retrieval_loop: MemoryStore.retrieve() keeps its gate order — gate 0 responsiveness (hashed record_terms, is_structural=0 real-content overlap), gate 1 tombstone responsiveness (tombstone_terms digests, is_structural=0), gate 2 role-grant match against role_grants, gate 3 relationship existence — and now, inside gate 3 instantiation, enforces the relationship's scope for routine records: when the requester's relationship to the patient has scope containing 'logistics' (stripped/lower), a routine-only record clears only if its kind is scheduling/portal_message/contact_line OR its body matches LOGISTICS_PATTERNS. Scope-enforced denials are written to access_log as deny_scope with reason 'scope: logistics_only' so the Critic audit path sees each firing. No tombstone and no non-routine sensitivity path changes behavior; the verbatim Details/logistics-suffix/rescue assembly is untouched because it reads decision.allowed, which now has fewer — never more — routine family rows.
forgetting_mechanism: Unchanged: tombstone() nulls body, purges record_terms into tombstone_terms (preserving is_structural digests for scoped gate-1 responsiveness), shreds the crypto key (crypto_keys.key_material=NULL, shredded_at set) so ciphertext is undecryptable; sanitize_and_decide branch 1 keeps tombstone-hit > everything so a responsive deletion forces no_memory; rescue_missing_logistics and _logistics_suffix read live cleared rows only and can never resurrect a tombstoned body. The deletion_request_audit table (SCHEMA_VERSION 7) remains the per-record post-mortem of which *_delete_*_line request matched which record; this iteration adds nothing to the deletion path and cannot move F off 0.
